title: Customer reference program: operational workflow (intake, HubSpot tracking, ownership, reporting)
creator: Camila Reyes
description:
Goal
Formalize and operationalize the *ongoing* customer reference workflow so Sales/CS can request references consistently without overburdening customers, and Marketing/RevOps can report on utilization + influence.

Scope (this ticket)
1) Define the standardized intake fields for requesting:
   - Reference call
   - Quote only
   - Logo approval only
   - Public case study (web + 1-pager)
2) HubSpot tracking changes:
   - Company + Deal properties to track eligibility, permissions, utilization, and outcomes
   - Lifecycle rules (who sets what, when)
3) Ownership rules + SLAs:
   - Required approvals (CSM/AE/Marketing/Legal)
   - Scheduling expectations + do-not-contact rules
   - Load management (caps/cooldowns)
4) Reporting requirements:
   - Reference-call utilization (requests/month, completed calls)
   - Case study pipeline influence (deal association + stage movement)
   - Health checks (overuse, negative feedback, opt-outs)

Non-goals
- Building the public-facing case study pages (tracked separately)
- Drafting the legal consent form language (owned by Legal; we only define the workflow touchpoints)

Background / context
We’re launching a case study + reference program targeting 3–5 design partners. We need a durable process that works after the initial 8–10 week push.
Key constraints:
- Some customers can do reference calls but won’t publish metrics/logos
- Need to avoid “surprise” asks and ensure AE/CS alignment
- Need to tag utilization so we can prove influence on late-stage conversion

Proposed workflow (v1)
A) Request intake (Sales/CS submits)
- Submits internal request (form or structured Slack + template) with required fields (see Intake Fields below)
- Must include CSM + AE names and confirm customer health check

B) Triage + approvals
- CSM approves customer readiness + confirms any current escalations
- AE confirms deal context + what the ask is (call vs quote vs public)
- Marketing confirms fit (story angle) + schedules interview/call logistics
- Legal approves if new permissions needed (logo/quote/metrics/public attribution)

C) Customer outreach + scheduling
- Outreach should come from the relationship owner (usually CSM; AE optional depending on account dynamics)
- Marketing provides approved ask language + incentive options if applicable
- Scheduling includes clear agenda, timebox, and boundaries (what we will/won’t cover)

D) Post-activity logging + follow-up
- Log completion + notes + next allowed date
- Attach brief + any customer constraints (“avoid list”)
- Trigger case study drafting workflow if applicable

E) Load management rules
- Default cap: max 2 reference calls/month per customer unless explicit opt-in
- Cooldown: 14 days between reference calls
- Immediate pause if customer expresses discomfort; escalation to CS leadership

Intake fields (required)
1) Request type: reference call | quote | logo | public case study
2) Prospect/deal context:
   - Deal name + link
   - Stage
   - Close date target
   - What is the prospect deciding (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, vendor swap, etc.)
3) Desired customer reference:
   - Company name
   - Primary contact + title
   - Backup contact
4) Story angle + proof points:
   - Latency/perf economics | reliability/fallbacks | deployment flexibility | ops tooling
   - Any specific metrics requested by prospect (ok if unknown)
5) Guardrails:
   - Topics to avoid
   - Known NDA/confidentiality constraints
   - Any recent escalations/incidents that could make the ask risky
6) Timing:
   - Ideal call date range
   - Hard deadline (if any)
   - Time zones
7) Approvals:
   - CSM approval checkbox
   - AE approval checkbox
   - If public use requested: Legal approval required
8) Incentive (if offered): Optimize trial extension | conference sponsorship credit | charitable donation

HubSpot changes (properties)
Company properties
- Reference status: Not eligible | Eligible | In rotation | Paused | Retired
- Reference types allowed: Calls | Quotes | Logo | Public case study (multi-select)
- Permissions on file: None | Verbal only | Signed consent (date)
- Max calls/month (default 2)
- Cooldown days (default 14)
- Last reference activity date
- Next eligible reference date
- Reference owner (CSM) + Secondary owner (AE)
- Narrative tags: Dedicated | Private/VPC | Hosted API | Optimize | Reliability/fallback | Cost reduction | Compliance/audit
- Metric disclosure: None | Ranges only | Exact metrics ok | Requires review per instance

Deal properties
- Reference needed: Yes/No
- Reference asset used: Call | Case study | 1-pager | Quote snippet
- Reference call completed date
- Reference influence: None | Low | Medium | High (self-reported by AE; guidance below)

Activity logging
- New activity type (or standardized note template): “Reference Call”
- Required fields in note template: attendees, Qs asked, what landed, follow-ups, any red flags, next eligible date

Ownership + RACI
- Requestor (AE/CSM): provides deal context + confirms readiness
- CSM (Rachel Kim’s org): final authority on customer readiness + load/cooldown enforcement
- Marketing Ops (Tyler Benson): intake QA + ensures HubSpot fields are filled + SLA tracking
- Marketing (Camila Reyes / Ethan Wallace): content execution (briefs, interviews, drafting)
- Solutions Eng (Markus Klein / Simran Kaur): technical validation + architecture diagrams
- Legal (Michael Grant / Sofia Mendes): consent, logo/quote/metrics permissions, redlines
- RevOps/CRM (Isabelle Laurent): property setup, reporting, dashboards

SLAs (internal)
- Triage: 1 business day to confirm if request is viable
- Scheduling: target 5 business days from approved request to scheduled slot (subject to customer availability)
- Post-call logging: within 24 hours of completion

Reporting requirements
Weekly (exec readout)
- # of new requests
- # scheduled / completed calls
- # customers in rotation, paused, retired
- # of case studies in draft / legal review / published
Monthly
- Utilization by segment (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
- Overuse flags (customers above cap, short cooldown violations)
- Pipeline influence: deals with reference asset used vs not, by stage

Acceptance criteria
- Intake fields documented and agreed by Sales + CS + Marketing Ops
- HubSpot property spec finalized (names, types, allowed values, ownership rules)
- Reporting definitions written (what counts as “reference used”, how to tag influence)
- Published internal workflow (Confluence) and announced in Slack
- First 2 reference requests run through the process with clean logging

Open questions
- Do we implement a form immediately, or start with a structured template + HubSpot task + Slack channel?
- Who is the single routing owner for triage: Marketing Ops vs CS Ops?
- Should we require a deal stage minimum (e.g., Stage 3+) for reference calls by default?

Implementation plan
- Week 1: finalize intake + ownership rules; align in cross-functional sync
- Week 2: implement HubSpot properties + views; draft reporting dashboard
- Week 2: publish Confluence workflow and announce process

Notes
- Default policy is “protect the customer relationship first.” If CS says no, it’s a no.
- For public case studies, we must have signed consent before publishing logo/quotes/metrics. Verbal approval is not sufficient.
comments: 2025-10-03 — Isabelle Laurent (CRM & utilization reporting): Drafted initial HubSpot spec. Suggest making Reference status a single-select with strict automation (Paused/Retired should prevent scheduling tasks). Also recommend a Deal-level property ‘Reference asset used’ to quantify influence beyond just activities.

2025-10-04 — Rachel Kim (CS readiness & approvals): +1 on load management. CS needs a hard cap and cooldown enforced in the process. Proposed guardrail: if account has an open Sev-1/Sev-2 or renewal risk flag, auto-pause reference asks until cleared. Also request that all outreach comes from CSM by default (Marketing can provide copy).

2025-10-07 — Tyler Benson (Marketing ops & intake tracking): Prefer lightweight v1: intake via a Google form OR Slack workflow that posts into #customer-references + creates a HubSpot task for the Reference owner. Form required fields will reduce back-and-forth. Can revisit a more complex request system later.

2025-10-09 — Avery Johnson (Enterprise AE): Sales needs clarity on lead time. Proposed guidance: request references at least 7 business days before target call date; include top 3 prospect questions so we prep the customer. Also asked whether we can allow exceptions to stage minimum for strategic accounts (answer: yes, but requires CS + Marketing approval).

2025-10-11 — Camila Reyes (Program owner): Confirmed v1 decision: start with form + Confluence page + HubSpot properties; keep scheduling managed by Marketing Ops but CSM has final go/no-go. Added policy: any customer can opt out at any time; opt-out logged as Retired (reason: customer request).

2025-10-15 — Isabelle Laurent: Implemented HubSpot properties in sandbox and shared screenshots. Open item: creating a saved view for ‘In rotation + next eligible date <= today’ for quick scheduling. Also needs Sales Ops to confirm where to store ‘Reference influence’ on deals (property vs playbook question).
2025-10-18 — Rachel Kim: Tested first request through workflow; logging looked good but asked to add a required field: ‘Topics to avoid’ (free text) + ‘Known compliance constraints’ (checkbox list).

2025-10-23 — Camila Reyes: Marking ready to close once Confluence page is updated with final property names and Slack announcement is posted. Reminder: the process must be usable by AEs who aren’t deep in the program—keep it minimal and link to templates.

2025-10-24 — Isabelle Laurent: Shipped HubSpot changes + published dashboard (internal). Confluence workflow updated and #announcements post scheduled. Closing as Done; follow-ups tracked in PM-1862 (form routing) and ongoing ops checklist.
